templateName: Blender refit + agent: fit an existing mesh, then refine it
description: Select ONE existing mesh (another model's output: .glb, .obj, .stl or .ply) together with the photograph it was made from. The scripted refit fits the mesh to the photograph first; the Blender agent then refines the refitted mesh, with the refit's report and the original mesh in its workspace. When the agent fails, the refit's result is delivered.
inputInstructions:
This template runs two things on a mesh another model made. First the scripted refit -- a fixed chain of Blender steps that turns the mesh to the photograph's view, warps its outline onto the photograph's, adds relief from a MoGe-2 depth estimate, brings it to the face count, checks it for leaks and projects the photograph onto it. Then the Blender agent (OpenAI Codex CLI, reasoning with a vision model on Amazon Bedrock) refines the refitted mesh, as on a refine run: it compares renders against the photograph, fixes what the photograph still contradicts, and fuses the result into one printable body.

The agent is handed the refit's report, its outline pictures before and after, and the mesh the refit started from, so it can return to the original where the refit made something worse. When the agent fails -- no exported model, a bridge that never starts -- the refit's result is delivered instead and the failure is recorded in the run report.

INPUT FILES. Select ONE mesh (.glb, .gltf, .obj, .stl or .ply) and the photograph it was made from. With several photographs the refit uses the first and the agent sees them all. The photograph must reach the refit cut out: Background removal none, or Image cleanup skip on a photograph with no transparent background, is refused before Blender starts, because the fit reads the subject's outline from the cutout. The agent's settings are checked before the refit starts, so a value the agent cannot use fails the run in seconds rather than after the refit.

GUIDANCE and BUDGET are the agent's, and its model and sandbox are fixed, exactly as on the refine template. The refit adds minutes to the run; the agent's budget and its model calls are still what dominates the cost.

Print readiness: with Mesh cleanup on, the result goes through the same decimation, repair, rescale and print gate as every other model. failClosed rejects the run when a check fails; bestEffort writes every output and records the results.

FORM. Each field is labelled with the stage that reads it, in the order a run executes them: [1 Input] prepares the photographs, [2 Generate] is this template's model, [3 Cleanup] repairs the mesh and brings it to the face count, [4 Colour] projects the photograph onto it, [5 Print] sizes it, adds print features and applies the print gate, and [6 Output] chooses the formats and reports. A template shows only the stages its model uses.

tagSchema.label: [1 Input] Image cleanup
tagSchema.description: auto segments the subject from its background, so the refit reads the subject's outline from the cutout and the agent receives both the photograph as supplied and the cutout. skip hands the photographs over exactly as supplied, which the refit accepts only when the first already has a transparent background.

tagSchema.label: [1 Input] Background removal
tagSchema.description: Segmentation model that cuts the subject out for the refit and for the agent's reference. The refit fits the mesh to the cutout's outline, so none is refused. birefnet keeps the most edge detail and picked the right subject where rembg did not, so select it unless the photograph is a clean studio shot. sam segments whatever SAM prompt points at, for a photograph holding several objects.

tagSchema.label: [1 Input] SAM prompt
tagSchema.description: Where to look, used only when Background removal is sam. centre takes the middle of the frame. x,y names a point and x0,y0,x1,y1 a box, as fractions of the image between 0 and 1.

tagSchema.label: [2 Generate] Rebuild the surface
tagSchema.description: How the reconstruction's surface is rebuilt before it is fitted. none keeps the reconstruction's own surface and its fine detail; voxel remeshes it as one even closed surface at the resolution below; metaball rebuilds it from overlapping spheres, which rounds thin parts and blunts points. A rebuild that moves the surface more than 2% of the subject's height on average, or keeps less of its volume than Minimum volume retained by a repair, is undone and the reason recorded.

tagSchema.label: [2 Generate] Rebuild resolution
tagSchema.description: The voxel size or sphere spacing of a rebuild, and of the leak check's last-resort remesh, as a fraction of the subject's height: 0.004 is 0.4 mm on a 10 cm print. Smaller keeps more detail and takes longer. Between 0.001 and 0.05.

tagSchema.label: [2 Generate] Fit the outline
tagSchema.description: Warp the mesh in the photograph's plane until its front outline matches the photograph's cutout, moving no part more than 3% of the subject's height. Set false for a subject whose straight edges matter more than its outline: a mug's rim and base can come out wavy where the fit followed the cutout's edge.

tagSchema.label: [2 Generate] Add relief from the photograph
tagSchema.description: Raise and lower the photographed side where a MoGe-2 depth estimate of the photograph shows detail the reconstruction smoothed away -- fur, folds, carved lines. Only what the camera sees moves, fading out towards the outline. Where the relief would make the surface cross itself it is held back, and it is undone if it still does.

tagSchema.label: [2 Generate] Relief depth
tagSchema.description: The most the relief moves the surface, as a fraction of the subject's height: 0.01 is a millimetre on a 10 cm print. 0 adds none. Between 0 and 0.05.

tagSchema.label: [2 Generate] Bring to the face count
tagSchema.description: How a mesh over Target face count is brought down to it. decimate collapses edges and keeps the surface's shape; quadriflow rebuilds it as even quads, which smooths fine detail, and falls back to decimate when it cannot remesh the surface. Target face count 0 leaves the face count as it is.

tagSchema.default: Keep the refitted mesh's body. Correct what the photograph still contradicts, then re-texture it from the photograph.
tagSchema.label: [2 Generate] Operator guidance
tagSchema.description: Free text passed to the agent verbatim, for what the photographs cannot say: the subject's real size, its material, what is on the side the camera did not see, which features matter most. Leave blank to let the agent work from the photographs alone.

tagSchema.label: [2 Generate] Max iterations
tagSchema.description: The most build-render-compare cycles the agent may run. It is told to finish inside this number, so the last two are spent baking, exporting and verifying rather than refining.

tagSchema.label: [2 Generate] Max minutes
tagSchema.description: Wall-clock budget for the agent. It is stopped a few minutes past this, and whatever it has exported by then is taken. A run that exports nothing fails.

tagSchema.label: [2 Generate] Reasoning effort
tagSchema.description: How much the model deliberates on each step. Higher is slower and costs more tokens, and produces more careful comparisons and fewer regressions. high for anything that will be printed; medium for a quick look.

tagSchema.label: [2 Generate] Render engine
tagSchema.description: The engine the agent renders its comparisons with. CYCLES is physically based and uses the GPU when one is present, falling back to the CPU; BLENDER_WORKBENCH is fast and flat, for geometry-only comparison; EEVEE needs a display-backed GL context that a headless container may not provide, and falls back to Cycles when it cannot start.

tagSchema.label: [2 Generate] Render samples
tagSchema.description: Cycles samples per comparison render. 32 is enough to judge shape and colour; raise it only if the agent reports noise confusing its comparison.

tagSchema.label: [3 Cleanup] Mesh cleanup
tagSchema.description: Run the print-readiness cleanup (decimate, repair, rescale, gate). Set false to return the mesh exactly as the agent exported it.

tagSchema.label: [3 Cleanup] Mesh repair ladder
tagSchema.description: Which repair backends the print-readiness cleanup may walk, least to most invasive. Applies only when Mesh cleanup is on.

tagSchema.label: [3 Cleanup] Minimum volume retained by a repair
tagSchema.description: Fraction of the mesh's original volume a repair step must leave behind for its result to be kept. The refit's rebuild is held to the same fraction.

tagSchema.label: [3 Cleanup] Largest hole the repair may close (edges)
tagSchema.description: Boundary size, in edges, of the largest hole the pymeshlab repair rung will close. 0 closes nothing.

tagSchema.label: [3 Cleanup] Target face count
tagSchema.description: Face budget the refit brings the mesh to before the agent starts, and the cleaned mesh is decimated to. 0 leaves the face count as it is.

tagSchema.label: [5 Print] Target size (mm)
tagSchema.description: Longest-edge size the mesh is rescaled to, in millimetres. Also told to the agent as the subject's real size. 0 leaves the agent's own scale untouched.

tagSchema.label: [5 Print] Print features
tagSchema.description: Parametric geometry added to the finished mesh for printing: loop for a hanging ring, base for a flat-bottomed stand, or both.

tagSchema.label: [5 Print] How the feature is attached
tagSchema.description: concat keeps the texture and leaves the feature as a second closed shell; union fuses one solid and discards the texture; auto picks per mesh.

tagSchema.label: [5 Print] Print feature colour
tagSchema.description: Flat colour given to added geometry, as #RRGGBB.

tagSchema.label: [5 Print] Loop hole diameter (mm)
tagSchema.description: Clear opening of the hanging loop, in millimetres. 0 sizes it to the model.

tagSchema.label: [5 Print] Loop thickness (mm)
tagSchema.description: Thickness of the loop's tube, in millimetres. 0 uses a fraction of the hole diameter.

tagSchema.label: [5 Print] Base diameter (mm)
tagSchema.description: Diameter of the stand base, in millimetres. 0 sizes it to the model's footprint.

tagSchema.label: [5 Print] Base height (mm)
tagSchema.description: Height of the stand base, in millimetres. 0 uses a fraction of the model's height.

tagSchema.label: [5 Print] Print gate policy
tagSchema.description: What happens when a print-readiness check fails. failClosed writes no mesh, only the gate report; bestEffort writes the outputs and records the failures. Prefer bestEffort while evaluating this path: an agent run is expensive and its result is worth seeing even when a check fails.

tagSchema.label: [6 Output] Export formats
tagSchema.description: Which containers the finished mesh is written as. glb carries geometry and texture in one file; obj writes the texture as a separate file set; stl is geometry only.

tagSchema.label: [6 Output] Benchmark report
tagSchema.description: Records per-stage timings and the hardware the run landed on into the run report. Switch it on when comparing this path against the reconstruction models: an agent run's cost is in its token counts and wall clock, and this is where they are recorded.

tagSchema.label: [6 Output] Pass the input photographs on
tagSchema.description: true copies the input photograph(s) into this run's outputs beside the mesh, so a later pipeline in the same workflow receives them together with the mesh. A workflow's second step is handed only the first step's outputs, so a reconstruct-then-refine workflow needs this on its first step. false leaves the outputs as the mesh, its formats and the reports.
